messages:
maya: Heads up — after bumping the FP8 calibration pass in the nightly build we saw a weird perf regression on long-seq workloads. P50 latency went from ~28ms to ~46ms and throughput dropped ~18%.

sam: ugh. which kernel path? Triton or CUTLASS?

maya: CUTLASS INT8 path mostly. We enabled the new per-channel calibration profile (auto-calib-v2) which nudges scale factors and triggers a different kernel selection in the runtime.

liam: quick note: the kernel selector heuristics switch to the INT8-specialized kernels when per-channel quantization density > 0.7. That threshold was hit after calib-v2.

anika: do we have flamegraphs / perf traces?

maya: uploaded a cpu/gpu profile to the perf bucket earlier: gs://redwood-perf/nightly/17642/calib-v2-cutlass-int8/. Main thing: increased stall in kernel launch queue + more memcpy-ish activity (KV cache reloads).

jamie: KV cache reloads? how does calibration affect KV behavior?

maya: hypothesis: changing scale factors changes token encoding sizes slightly which alters batching grouping and forces more frequent KV cache evictions for long context users. When a batch includes both cached prefixes and uncached requests we end up in mixed-mode slow paths.

sam: that matches a trace I saw — mixed-batch branch in runtime hits a fallback memcpy that serializes streams.

liam: also noticed CUTLASS kernel for 4-bit fallback on Ampere had suboptimal block sizes with the new flags, Hopper was fine. Could be arch-detect mismatch.

anika: are we doing arch autodetect at runtime or compile-time?

liam: both — we compile multiple codepaths and runtime selects by reported SM. But the build flag FAST_MATH_TUNED=true flips some tiling heuristics at compile time that our selector assumes only Hopper supports. On Ampere it picks a kernel that regresses.

maya: repro steps I ran (quick):
```bash
# run the eval harness with calib-v2 and cutlass-int8 on Ampere node
python -m harness.run --model gpt-neox-20b --quant int8 --calib auto-calib-v2 --node ampere-a100-40gb --batch 8 --seq 2048
```

maya: attach: short log snippet ->
```
[ RUN ] batch=8 seq=2048 model=gpt-neox-20b quant=int8
cutlass_kernel=sm_80_int8_tileA1024_T1 chosen
kv_cache_evictions=12
kernel_queue_depth=1 -> throttle
P50=46.3ms P95=312ms
```

jamie: interesting that queue depth drops to 1. sounds like stream serialization as Sam said. Is there a fallback memcpy gate in kvcache path?

sam: yes, when mixed cached/un-cached we currently run sequential copies to preserve KV index order. We added that as a conservatism, but maybe can convert to async copies + barriers.

anika: two actionable hypotheses: (1) calibration causes selector to choose an Ampere-unfriendly CUTLASS kernel due to FAST_MATH_TUNED compile flag; (2) runtime mixed-batch memcpy serializes streams causing queue depth collapse. We can mitigate (2) faster at runtime; (1) needs a selector guard or rebuild without that flag.

liam: I can add a runtime guard: if SM < 90 and kernel_tiling == T1 then prefer generic int8 kernel. Quick patch: change kernel_selector.cpp line ~421 to bump score for generic kernels on Ampere.

maya: can you also add a toggle env var REDWOOD_FORCE_GENERIC_INT8=true for immediate canary?

liam: yeah will push a canary to staging now.

jamie: for (2) I can prototype async memcpy with cudaMemcpyAsync + stream-per-batch and then cudaEventSynchronize before kernel launch. If that keeps stream parallelism, should recover queue depth.

sam: we should also record a regression job matrix crossing: {ampere,hopper} x {calib-v1,calib-v2} x {cutlass-int8,triton-int8,4bit}. Add to CI perf nightly so we don't regress silently.

anika: agree. add perf thresholds: P50 must not increase >12% vs baseline for seq>=1024. If it does, auto-open perf-alert.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/runtime/1764200067 -> staging at 2026-03-18T10:24:00Z (liam) :rocket:

maya: thanks. post-canary checklist:
- check ampere staging P50/P95 numbers for seq 512/1024/2048
- validate KV eviction rate drops
- verify kernel selection logs show generic-int8 on Ampere when env toggle set

liam: working on it, will ping here with results in ~30m.

jamie: if we confirm, followup: plan a permanent fix — either adjust compile flags per-arch or make selector aware of FAST_MATH_TUNED implications. Long-term maybe add a small micro-benchmark at startup to pick fastest kernel variant per node.

maya: micro-benchmark sounds ideal. low-risk rollout: default to selector heuristics, allow per-node cached best-variant after 1k micro-requests.

sam: sweet. also document in eng-runtime README the gotcha about FAST_MATH_TUNED and architecture assumptions. :+1:

liam: canary logs: staging run summary -> ampere P50 seq=2048 with env toggle=true -> 29.1ms, kv_evictions=3, kernel_queue_depth=6. Looks promising.

maya: awesome, that basically recovers baseline. thanks team.

anika: filing followup tickets: PERF-3377 (selector guard), PERF-3378 (async kvcache copies), PERF-3379 (micro-benchmark per-node).

maya: closing loop here once we merge patches. :wave:
